seoTitle: Fix Black Highlight Covers & Edit Them on Instagram PC
metaDescription: Fix Instagram highlight covers appearing as a solid black box, and edit highlight covers directly from your computer.
intro: A highlight cover that shows up as a flat black square instead of your photo is one of the more annoying small glitches on Instagram, and it tends to show up right when you're trying to tidy up a profile for followers or clients. Most of the time it isn't a broken account at all: it's a stuck cache on the device you're editing from, or a cover image uploaded in a shape Instagram doesn't like. This guide covers the actual fix — finding the Edit Cover option buried in the highlight's menu, clearing the app data that's usually the real culprit, and what to do if you're trying to sort this out from a computer instead of your phone.

steps.heading: Open the highlight and choose Edit Cover
steps.body:
Long-press the highlight bubble showing the black cover, or open the highlight and tap the three-dot menu while it's playing. A sheet slides up from the bottom listing Remove from Highlight, Edit Highlight, Send, Boost Story, Share to Facebook story, and Archive Highlight. Tap Edit Highlight.

Inside that screen, look for a separate Edit Cover button next to the filmstrip of stories already in the highlight. It's a distinct step from picking which stories belong in the highlight, and it's the one that swaps the cover image without touching the stories themselves. Removing and rebuilding the whole highlight is not necessary just to fix a broken cover.

image.caption: The highlight's action sheet, with Edit Highlight sitting between Remove from Highlight and Send. This is the menu that leads to Edit Cover.

steps.heading: Clear the app's cache before you re-upload
steps.body:
If the cover still renders black after re-selecting an image, the usual cause is a stale cache holding onto a corrupted thumbnail rather than the file itself. How you clear it depends on the platform, and the two are not the same task.

On Android, open the phone's own Settings, go to Apps, select Instagram, and tap Storage. You'll see separate Total, App, Data, and Cache figures, and a dedicated Clear cache button that only removes temporary files without touching your login or posts.

iOS has no equivalent per-app cache control, and Instagram hasn't built one into its iPhone app either. The nearest thing is offloading the app: Settings, General, iPhone Storage, Instagram, then Offload App. This clears the app's stored data while keeping your documents, and reopening (or reinstalling) Instagram rebuilds it fresh.

image.caption: The app storage screen on Android, showing Instagram's cache figure separately from its app and data size, with a dedicated Clear cache button.

steps.heading: Re-upload the cover in the right shape, then check your profile
steps.body:
With the cache cleared, go back into Edit Cover and choose a new image. Instagram crops highlight covers into a circle, so use a square or near-square source and center whatever needs to stay visible. A wide landscape photo gets cropped unpredictably, which is its own way of making a cover look broken even once the black-box glitch is gone.

Save the change and back out to your profile. Your highlights sit in a row just under your bio and stats, with a plus-sign circle for new ones followed by your existing covers in order. That row is the fastest place to confirm the fix actually took, since a leftover black cover will be obvious next to every other thumbnail displaying fine.

image.caption: The profile highlights row beneath the bio, where every highlight cover is listed side by side — the fastest place to confirm whether the fix worked.

steps.heading: Still black? Try a different device
steps.body: Occasionally the glitch is tied to one specific app build or session instead of the cache. If clearing cache and re-uploading hasn't fixed it, repeat the edit from a different device: a computer browser if you were on a phone, or a second phone if one's available. Once the cover displays correctly there, switch back to your primary device; it typically syncs and resolves on its own within a few minutes.

tables.title: Clearing Instagram's cache by platform
rows: Settings > Apps > Instagram > Storage > Clear cache
No per-app cache control exists. Settings > General > iPhone Storage > Instagram > Offload App, then reopen or reinstall Instagram.
tables.note: Offloading keeps your Instagram login and documents; only the cached files are cleared.

troubleshooting.problem: There's no Clear Cache button anywhere on my phone
troubleshooting.cause: You're on iPhone. iOS doesn't expose a per-app cache control the way Android does, and Instagram hasn't added its own.
troubleshooting.fix: Use Offload App instead: Settings > General > iPhone Storage > Instagram > Offload App, then reopen Instagram and check the highlight again.

troubleshooting.problem: The cover reverts to black immediately after saving
troubleshooting.cause: The uploaded image was cropped from a wide, non-square source, or the upload was interrupted mid-save by a weak connection.
troubleshooting.fix: Re-upload a square, high-contrast image on a stable connection, and wait for the highlight preview to render before backing out of Edit Cover.

troubleshooting.problem: The cover looks fine on my phone but blank on a computer
troubleshooting.cause: Instagram's browser tools for highlights are more limited than the app's, and cover thumbnails there can lag behind a change just made on mobile.
troubleshooting.fix: Treat the phone app as the source of truth for this fix. Refresh or reopen the browser tab a few minutes after saving on mobile rather than troubleshooting the desktop view directly.

faq.question: Why does my highlight cover show as a black box?
faq.answer: Almost always a stale local cache holding a broken thumbnail, or a cover image uploaded in a shape the app struggled to crop. Clearing the cache and re-uploading resolves it in most cases.

faq.question: Where do I find the option to change just the cover, not the whole highlight?
faq.answer: Long-press the highlight bubble or open its three-dot menu, choose Edit Highlight, then look for Edit Cover inside that screen. It swaps only the cover image and leaves the stories in the highlight untouched.

faq.question: Will clearing my cache delete my Instagram data?
faq.answer: No. Clearing cache only removes temporary files like cached thumbnails; it doesn't touch your login, posts, or saved data. On iPhone, the closest option is Offload App, which behaves the same way.

faq.question: What shape should a highlight cover image be?
faq.answer: Square or near-square, since Instagram crops highlight covers into a circle. Wide or oddly shaped source images crop unpredictably and can make a fixed cover look broken again.

faq.question: I'm on an iPhone and there's no Clear Cache button. Now what?
faq.answer: iOS doesn't have one. Offload the app instead through Settings > General > iPhone Storage > Instagram > Offload App, then reopen Instagram and check the highlight.

faq.question: Can I fix this, or edit highlights at all, from a computer?
faq.answer: You can view and organize highlights from instagram.com in a browser, but its cover-editing tools are thinner than the app's and can lag behind a mobile change. For the actual fix in this guide, the phone app is the more reliable place to work; use the browser to double-check afterward, not to make the edit itself.

They were instead cross-checked against several independent 2026 support guides: the iPhone/Android difference in clearing cache (iOS has no per-app Clear Cache control and needs Offload App instead) was the correction that came out of that check, and a step on desktop/browser editing was added to match what this article's own title promises.
